newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends quiet session slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends quiet session slightly higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices ended slightly higher in subdued pre-holiday trade, with light speculative buying helping to fuel minor gains, dealers said.
Arabica prices hovered in positive territory for the bulk of Monday's session, after a robust rally on Friday helped shore up the market's technical outlook.
But the market was unable to carve out new ground today, staying well within the previous session's ranges.
Most-active March delivery rose 0.95 cent a lb on the day, to 113.10 cents, while May gained 1.00 cent, to 110.60.
The day's turnover reached a meager 3,971 lots.

Technically, March would need to pierce through Friday's high of 113.90 to give the market further impetus, with 115 seen as a crucial upside objective. Underneath the market, 110.50 cents was an important support level, followed by 109 and 105.

Stock data released after the close of trading Monday showed a sharp build in CSCE certified coffee inventories. Certified coffee stocks jumped by a whopping 21,744 60-kg bags as of December 20, to 34,315 bags, led by increases in Guatemalan and Venezuelan supplies.
CSCE has scheduled a half-day session for December 24, with coffee futures trading slated to close at 1135 EST/1635 GMT. The exchange is closed on Christmas Day, December 25.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
